title: transform
body:
## transform

Places a copy of the input mesh by composing translation, rotation (XYZ Euler, degrees) and scale on top of the input object's world transform: world = T * R * S * input. Scale and rotation therefore act about the world origin, not the part's own centre. The mesh vertices are not changed; only the object transform is, so later modifiers still work in the original local coordinates unless you add applyTransform.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- A part centred away from the origin moves when scaled or rotated; translate it to the origin first or apply the transform before it is offset.
- Rotation is in degrees here, whereas bend and twist angles are radians.

Native binding: `transform`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | one node | yes | `data` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `translation` | Displacement [x, y, z] added after rotation and scale, in world axes. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `rotation` | Rotation angles [x, y, z] in degrees, applied as a Blender XYZ Euler rotation (about X first, then Y, then Z) about the world origin, after scale and before translation. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `scale` | Scale factors [x, y, z] along the world axes about the world origin, applied before rotation; all must be positive. Use 0.001 on every axis to bring millimetre data to metre-sized Blender units. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[1,1,1]` |
